title: Chad Channing - Wikipedia
notes: Nirvana's drummer 1988-1990, on Bleach and 'Polly' on Nevermind; Dale Crover drums 'Floyd the Barber' and 'Paper Cuts' from earlier sessions; Grohl adapted Channing's parts for many songs; Incesticide credits him on 'Dive', 'Stain', 'Big Long Now'.

title: Chuck Biscuits - Wikipedia
notes: Charles Montgomery, b. 17 April 1965. D.O.A. 1978-1982 (first two albums), Black Flag briefly, Circle Jerks, Danzig 1987-1994 (first four albums; Glenn Danzig's first choice), Social Distortion 1996-1999. Influences: Bonham, Rat Scabies, Topper Headon, Keith Moon, Stewart Copeland.

title: Clem Burke - Wikipedia
notes: Clement Burke (Bozewski), 24 Nov 1954 - 6 April 2025, Bayonne NJ. Blondie 1975-2025 on every album; 'Elvis Ramone' for two Ramones gigs in 1987; the Romantics 1990-2004; sessions with Eurythmics, Dylan, Iggy Pop. Drum and bugle corps background; influenced by Hal Blaine, Keith Moon, Ringo Starr, Earl Palmer.

title: Clive Deamer - Wikipedia
notes: English drummer. Hawkwind 1983-85; Portishead since 1994 (Dummy, Portishead, Roseland NYC Live, Third); Roni Size & Reprazent's Mercury-winning New Forms (1997); Get the Blessing since 2000; Radiohead's second drummer on The King of Limbs and A Moon Shaped Pool tours. Selway: 'One played in the traditional way, the other almost mimicked a drum machine.'

title: Dale Crover - Wikipedia
notes: b. 23 Oct 1967. Melvins' drummer since 1984 and with Buzz Osborne the only constant member; on Nirvana's January 1988 ten-song demo, three songs of which are on Bleach; Rolling Stone's 69th greatest drummer (2016). Osborne referred Cobain to Dave Grohl.

title: D. H. Peligro - Wikipedia
notes: Darren Henley, 9 July 1959 - 28 Oct 2022. Dead Kennedys from Feb 1981 (In God We Trust, Inc.; Plastic Surgery Disasters; Frankenchrist; Bedtime for Democracy); Red Hot Chili Peppers in 1988, replacing Jack Irons.

title: Earl Hudson - Wikipedia
notes: b. 17 Dec 1957, Alabama. Bad Brains' drummer, younger brother of singer H.R.; rarely recorded outside the band.

title: Bad Brains - Wikipedia
notes: Washington DC; Dr. Know, Darryl Jenifer, Earl and Paul 'H.R.' Hudson. Hardcore punk and reggae; Rolling Stone: 'the mother of all black hard-rock bands'; cited as a seminal influence on hardcore and on thrash, alternative and funk metal. H.R. and Earl left in 1987 to focus on reggae.

title: Jerry Nolan - Wikipedia
notes: Gerard Nolan, 7 May 1946 - 14 Jan 1992, Brooklyn. Joined the New York Dolls in autumn 1972 after Billy Murcia's death; the Heartbreakers with Johnny Thunders; backed Sid Vicious in New York in 1978.

title: Marky Ramone - Wikipedia
notes: Marc Bell, b. 15 July 1952. Dust, Estus, Richard Hell and the Voidoids; Ramones 1978-1983 and 1987-1996, their longest-serving drummer. On the Dolls audition: 'I basically overplayed it... And Jerry just kept the beat straight.'

title: Jim Sclavunos - Wikipedia
notes: Brooklyn. Drummer of the seminal no wave groups Teenage Jesus & the Jerks and 8 Eyed Spy with Lydia Lunch, 'helping to kick-start' no wave; drums on part of Sonic Youth's Confusion Is Sex; the Cramps; Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds since 1994; founder of Grinderman.

title: The Charlatans (English band) - Wikipedia
notes: Formed 1988 in the West Midlands by Martin Blunt with Rob Collins, Jon Brookes (drums), Jon Day; Tim Burgess on vocals. Sound 'characterised by Collins's Hammond organ, underpinned by the driving rhythm section'; associated with Madchester. Brookes collapsed on stage in Philadelphia in 2010.

title: John Maher (Buzzcocks drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: b. 21 April 1960. Joined Buzzcocks at 16 in 1976; punk and new wave scenes in Manchester; Flag of Convenience; Wah!; left after the 1989 reunion tour; returned for two shows in 2012.

title: Kenny Morris (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: 1 Feb 1957 - 15 Jan 2026. First studio drummer of Siouxsie and the Banshees (Feb 1977 - Sept 1979): The Scream (1978), Join Hands (1979). 'Noted for playing mostly tom-toms and hardly using hi-hat'; cited as an influence by Stephen Morris and Kevin Haskins; 'Metal Postcard' sampled by Massive Attack (1997). Lillywhite recorded his kick and snare first, cymbals and toms later, on 'Hong Kong Garden'.

title: Moe Tucker - Wikipedia
notes: Maureen Tucker, b. 26 Aug 1944, Queens. The Velvet Underground's drummer; played standing, on a simplified kit of toms, snare and an upturned bass drum, with mallets, and rarely used cymbals, holding a drummer's job was to 'keep time'. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 1996.

title: Pete de Freitas - Wikipedia
notes: 2 Aug 1961 - 14 June 1989. Joined Echo & the Bunnymen in 1979, replacing a drum machine; on their first five albums. McCulloch: told 'to get stuck into the toms. Budgie ... was the only other drummer doing that stuff at the time and Pete loved his drumming'.

title: Reed Mullin - Wikipedia
notes: 12 Feb 1966 - 27 Jan 2020, Raleigh. Co-founder and drummer of Corrosion of Conformity, which moved from hardcore punk to southern, sludge and stoner metal with Blind (1991); left 2001, rejoined 2010.

title: Unwound - Wikipedia
notes: Olympia, Washington noise rock/post-hardcore band. Sara Lund replaced Brandt Sandeno in July 1992 and played on the debut (1993); the Lund-Trosper-Rumsey trio recorded seven albums until 2002; 'frequently been seen as one of the most influential bands of the 1990s'; with Sleater-Kinney, Kill Rock Stars' flagship bands.

title: Steve White (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 May 1965. Learned from Buddy Rich and Louie Bellson records; joined Paul Weller's Style Council in 1983 at 17 for his jazz background; youngest drummer on stage at Live Aid (1985); with Weller for many years; brother of Oasis's Alan White.

title: Terry Chimes - Wikipedia
notes: b. 5 July 1956. Original drummer of the Clash; recorded the debut album The Clash, credited as Tory Crimes; returned 1982-83; Generation X, Hanoi Rocks, Black Sabbath 1987-88; Rock Hall 2003.

title: Thomas Wydler - Wikipedia
notes: Swiss, b. 9 Oct 1959. Founder of Die Haut (1982); Bad Seeds drummer since 1985, debut on Kicking Against the Pricks (1986); sole drummer until Sclavunos joined in 1994; Wydler usually plays kit while Sclavunos plays auxiliary percussion.

title: William Goldsmith - Wikipedia
notes: b. 4 July 1972, Seattle. Sunny Day Real Estate, whose two Sub Pop albums 'brought about newfound popularity for the emo genre'; Foo Fighters 1995-1997 (most of his Colour and the Shape parts re-recorded by Grohl). Keith Moon his biggest influence.

title: Christian Grahn - Wikipedia
notes: b. 12 June 1978. The Hives' drummer; known for high-speed, accurate drumming; on Tyrannosaurus Hives plays machine-like rhythms, splitting the left hand between snare and tom under hi-hat eighths ('Two-Timing Touch and Broken Bones'), unbroken fast 16ths on 'A Little More for Little You'.

title: A Certain Ratio - Wikipedia
notes: Manchester post-punk band, 1977; Donald Johnson on drums from 1979. 'One of the first indie groups to draw heavy influence from funk as well as disco and Latin percussion'; early Factory Records act; New York stay increased Latin, jazz and Cuban percussion on Sextet.

title: Jon Theodore - Wikipedia
notes: b. 30 Dec 1973. 'Explosive, multi-textural playing style'; the Mars Volta 2001-2006 (De-Loused in the Comatorium, Frances the Mute, Amputechture); Queens of the Stone Age since 2013; Haitian descent influenced his drumming patterns.

title: Joey Castillo - Wikipedia
notes: b. 30 March 1966, Gardena. Wasted Youth; Danzig 1994-2002 (Chuck Biscuits's drum tech, then his replacement); Queens of the Stone Age 2002-2012 (Lullabies to Paralyze, Era Vulgaris, half of ...Like Clockwork); Circle Jerks. Influences War, Al Green, Zeppelin, Black Flag.

title: Josh Freese - Wikipedia
notes: b. 25 Dec 1972. The Vandals since 1989, A Perfect Circle 1999-2012 and since 2024, Devo 1996-2023, Guns N' Roses 1997-1999, Foo Fighters 2023-2025; over 400 albums since 1986 (NIN, Weezer, Sting...). Variety: 'one of the most in-demand session drummers in the business'.

title: Scott Raynor - Wikipedia
notes: b. 23 May 1978. Founding drummer of Blink-182 at 14: Buddha (1994), Cheshire Cat (1995), the gold-certified Dude Ranch (1997); replaced by Travis Barker in 1998.

title: Ilan Rubin - Wikipedia
notes: b. 7 July 1988. Lostprophets 2006-08, Nine Inch Nails, Paramore, Angels & Airwaves; Rock Hall 2020 with NIN as its youngest living inductee; Foo Fighters from 2025, replacing Josh Freese.

title: Matt Cameron - Wikipedia
notes: b. 28 Nov 1962. Soundgarden 1986-1997, 2010-2017; Pearl Jam 1998-2025; Temple of the Dog. Rolling Stone's 52nd greatest drummer. 'The task of figuring out the time signatures for Soundgarden's songs was usually left to Cameron'; 'uncanny ability to make odd time feel like straight time'; ghost-note grooves.

title: Stephen Perkins - Wikipedia
notes: b. 13 Sept 1967. Jane's Addiction from 1985, Porno for Pyros; 'his style blends rock, jazz, swing, African, Indian and Latin drumming styles'; added percussion to his kit in search of new sounds.

title: Mark Brzezicki - Wikipedia
notes: b. 21 June 1957, Slough. Big Country's drummer; session drummer for Pete Townshend (Empty Glass), Anni-Frid Lyngstad (Shine), the Cult, Ultravox, Procol Harum and many more.

title: Bill Stevenson (American musician) - Wikipedia
notes: b. 10 Sept 1963, Torrance. Drummer, main songwriter and only constant member of the Descendents; Black Flag from Dec 1981 to 1985 on five studio albums 'including the highly influential My War'; ALL; co-founder of the Blasting Room studio.

title: Robo (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Julio Roberto Valverde, b. 1955, Cali, Colombia. Black Flag's second drummer 1978-1981 (Jealous Again, Six Pack, Damaged), then the Misfits. 'Robo's drum style relies heavily on open high-hat to generate the frenetic sounds on early Black Flag records.'

title: Tommy Ramone - Wikipedia
notes: Tamás Erdélyi, 29 Jan 1949 - 11 July 2014, Budapest. Meant to manage the Ramones, he took the drums because 'nobody else wanted to'; drummer 1974-1978 on and co-producer of Ramones, Leave Home, Rocket to Russia and It's Alive.

title: Rat Scabies - Wikipedia
notes: Christopher Millar, b. 30 July 1955. Founded the Damned in 1976; they released 'New Rose', the first punk single in the UK; with the band until 1995.

title: Jet Black - Wikipedia
notes: Brian Duffy, 26 Aug 1938 - 6 Dec 2022. Founding drummer of the Stranglers; style 'usually simple and jazz-influenced'; moved to an electronic Simmons kit in the studio on Feline and Aural Sculpture; patented the 'Jet Black Power Bass Drum Pedal'.

title: Scott Asheton - Wikipedia
notes: 16 Aug 1949 - 15 March 2014. Co-formed the Stooges in 1967; 'The primitive sound that Asheton made was a template for many punk bands to come.'

title: Dennis Thompson (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: 7 Sept 1948 - 9 May 2024, Detroit. MC5 from 1965; nicknamed 'Machine Gun' for his 'assault' style of fast, hard-hitting drumming that 'pre-figured and influenced punk, metal, and hardcore punk drumming styles'. Influences Elvin Jones, Keith Moon, Mitch Mitchell, Motown.

title: Billy Ficca - Wikipedia
notes: b. 15 Feb 1950. Founding drummer of the Neon Boys and Television with Tom Verlaine and Richard Hell, later the Waitresses.

title: Jay Dee Daugherty - Wikipedia
notes: b. 22 March 1952. With Patti Smith from 1975 after a stint as her sound man; Tom Verlaine's solo records; CBGB's house band.

title: Chris Frantz - Wikipedia
notes: b. 8 May 1951. Co-founder and drummer of Talking Heads and Tom Tom Club; Rock Hall 2002; No. 12 in Stylus Magazine's 50 greatest rock drummers; known as an influence on the jam band scene after Phish covered Remain in Light.

title: Alan Myers (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: 29 Dec 1954 - 24 June 2013, Akron. Jazz background; joined Devo in 1976 on an acoustic kit; the Devo drummer most associated with the band; left as drum machines took over.

title: Pete Thomas (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: b. 9 Aug 1954. Drummer of Elvis Costello's Attractions and Costello's solo work; Squeeze in the 1990s; Tom Waits: 'one of the best rock drummers alive'; idol Mitch Mitchell.

title: Gina Schock - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 Aug 1957, Baltimore. Drummer of the Go-Go's from 1979; Edie and the Eggs before; self-taught; noted for 'powerful drumming technique'; Rock Hall 2021.

title: Palmolive (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Paloma Romero, b. 26 Dec 1954, Melilla, Spain. Founded the Slits in 1976, having never played an instrument; 'Palmolive's passionate drumming was key to the overall brashness' of the group; Peel sessions 1977-78; then the Raincoats' first album (1979).

title: Hugo Burnham - Wikipedia
notes: b. 25 March 1956. Gang of Four, formed at Leeds in 1977. Greil Marcus: 'economical and precise yet propulsive style, giving the rhythm a piston-like drive'.

title: Martin Atkins - Wikipedia
notes: b. 3 Aug 1959, Coventry. Public Image Ltd from 1979 (Metal Box, The Flowers of Romance), Ministry (dual drums with Bill Rieflin), Nine Inch Nails (Broken), Killing Joke; founder of Pigface; runs the Museum of Post Punk and Industrial Music.

title: Paul Ferguson - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 March 1958. Founding Killing Joke drummer 1979-1987 and again from 2008; 'known for his tribal drum style'.

title: Lol Tolhurst - Wikipedia
notes: b. 3 Feb 1959. Founder member of the Cure; drums on their first four albums, then keyboards after the Pornography tour (1982); co-host with Budgie of the Curious Creatures podcast.

title: Boris Williams - Wikipedia
notes: b. 24 April 1951. The Cure's drummer 1984-1994, from The Head on the Door; 'often cited by fans as the best drummer in the band's history'; Freaky Trigger: 'willingness to create an entire beat based on doing rolls on the various toms'.

title: Kevin Haskins - Wikipedia
notes: b. 19 July 1960. Bauhaus, 'generally regarded as the first Gothic rock group'; Tones on Tail; Love and Rockets. Influences: Stephen Morris's 16ths on the hi-hat and Synare, Kenny Morris's toms instead of hi-hats and cymbals.

title: Bill Berry - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 July 1958. R.E.M.'s drummer until 1997, 'best known for his economical drumming style'; songwriting contributions to 'Everybody Hurts' and 'Man on the Moon'.

title: Steve Shelley - Wikipedia
notes: b. 23 June 1962. Sonic Youth's drummer 1985-2011; founded Smells Like Records; drums on Cat Power's first three albums; Sun Kil Moon.

title: Georgia Hubley - Wikipedia
notes: b. 9 Feb 1957. One of the two founding members of Yo La Tengo (1984) with Ira Kaplan; drummer and vocalist; first album Ride the Tiger (1986).

title: Yo La Tengo - Wikipedia
notes: Hoboken indie band formed by Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley in 1984; lineup since 1992 Kaplan, Hubley (drums, vocals), James McNew.

title: Janet Weiss - Wikipedia
notes: b. 24 Sept 1965. Quasi, Sleater-Kinney, Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks, Wild Flag. Rolling Stone's 90th greatest drummer (2016); Stylus 48th; self-taught from Bonham and Topper Headon; a beat so solid 'you could practically bang your head against it'.

title: Patty Schemel - Wikipedia
notes: b. 24 April 1967. Hole's drummer 1992-1998, on Live Through This (1994); replaced by a session player on Celebrity Skin.

title: David Lovering - Wikipedia
notes: b. 6 Dec 1961. Pixies' drummer from 1986; his contribution on 'Bone Machine' (opening drum solo), 'Break My Body' and 'River Euphrates' 'established his steady, accurate style'; influences Rush, Steely Dan, Zeppelin, Devo.

title: Jimmy Chamberlin - Wikipedia
notes: b. 10 June 1964. Smashing Pumpkins' drummer; trained as a jazz drummer (Krupa, Rich, Ellington); Rolling Stone's 53rd greatest drummer (2016).

title: Brendan Canty - Wikipedia
notes: b. 9 March 1966. Deadline (1981), Rites of Spring, Fugazi; Stylus Magazine's No. 29 of the '50 Greatest Rock Drummers' (2007); a large farmer's bell in his kit.

title: Jeff Nelson (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: b. 1962. Minor Threat's drummer; co-founded Dischord Records with Ian MacKaye in 1980.

title: Minor Threat - Wikipedia
notes: Washington DC hardcore band formed 1980 by Ian MacKaye and drummer Jeff Nelson; all recordings released on their own Dischord Records.

title: George Hurley - Wikipedia
notes: b. 4 Sept 1958. Minutemen and fIREHOSE; self-taught; 'although he is known as a punk drummer, Hurley's musical influences are primarily jazz-based' (Max Roach).

title: Lucky Lehrer - Wikipedia
notes: b. 18 April 1958, LA. Jazz-trained; Circle Jerks, Redd Kross, Bad Religion, Darby Crash Band. 'An early developer of hardcore punk drumming... called the Godfather of hardcore drumming'; Flipside's best punk drummer of all time; syncopated style from jazz and Latin drumming.

title: Tobi Vail - Wikipedia
notes: b. 20 July 1969, Olympia. Founding drummer of Bikini Kill; 'a central figure in the riot grrrl scene—she coined the spelling of grrrl'; zine Jigsaw.

title: Dan Peters - Wikipedia
notes: b. 18 Aug 1967. Mudhoney's drummer since 1988 (Superfuzz Bigmuff on); Nirvana's drummer for 'Sliver' (1990); Screaming Trees 1990-91.

title: Sean Kinney - Wikipedia
notes: b. 27 May 1966, Renton. Co-founder and only drummer of Alice in Chains; nine Grammy nominations with the band; cut off his cast to record Facelift.

title: Tré Cool - Wikipedia
notes: Frank Wright III, b. 9 Dec 1972. Green Day from 1990; the intro to 'Basket Case' ranked among the best drum fills; adopted 'a more rhythmic style with fewer drum fills' to match Mike Dirnt's bass.

title: Britt Walford - Wikipedia
notes: b. 16 March 1970, Louisville. Drummer and co-founder of post-rock band Slint; Squirrel Bait; drums on the Breeders' Pod as 'Shannon Doughton'.

title: John McEntire - Wikipedia
notes: b. 9 April 1970. Drummer, multi-instrumentalist and engineer of Tortoise and the Sea and Cake; Bastro; 'a pioneering user of modern digital audio workstation software' (Pro Tools on The Fawn and Stereolab's Dots and Loops, 1997).

title: Damon Che - Wikipedia
notes: b. 15 Feb 1968, Pittsburgh. Don Caballero, 'math rock pioneers', since 1991; 'his drumming takes more of a lead instrument role than just keeping time', guitars as the rhythmic foundation while he soloed; four 'highly influential albums' 1993-2000.

title: Zach Hill - Wikipedia
notes: b. 28 Dec 1979. Drummer of math rock band Hella (from 2001) and drummer-producer of Death Grips; Modern Drummer feature, Aug 2006.

title: Brian Chippendale - Wikipedia
notes: b. 22 July 1973. Drummer and vocalist of noise rock duo Lightning Bolt (sings through a contact mic); drums on Björk's Volta; Rolling Stone's 91st greatest drummer (2016).

title: Glenn Kotche - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 Dec 1970. Wilco from Yankee Hotel Foxtrot on; solo percussion albums Next and Mobile; composed for the Kronos Quartet (Anomaly) and So Percussion; Gigwise's 40th greatest drummer.

title: Meg White - Wikipedia
notes: b. 10 Dec 1974. Drummer of the White Stripes 1997-2011; 'a key artist of the 2000s indie and garage rock movements, noted for her minimalist drumming style'; her drumming 'initially polarized critics but has since become highly regarded'; NME and Rolling Stone rank her among the greatest drummers.

title: Fabrizio Moretti - Wikipedia
notes: b. 2 June 1980, Rio de Janeiro. The Strokes' drummer since their 2001 debut; style 'crisp and clean'; a steady, driving force on a four-piece kit; Little Joy.

title: Matt Tong - Wikipedia
notes: b. 29 April 1979, Bournemouth. Bloc Party 2002-2013; wrote the Silent Alarm drum parts alternating high and low intensity; Algiers since 2015.

title: Colm Ó Cíosóig - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 Oct 1964, Irish. My Bloody Valentine's drummer; Isn't Anything (1988) and Loveless (1991) 'established Ó Cíosóig as a pioneering figure in the shoegaze genre'; 'energetic and snare-heavy drumming'; on Loveless his patterns were sampled and re-arranged.

title: Loz Colbert - Wikipedia
notes: b. 27 June 1970. Ride's drummer (Nowhere, Going Blank Again); the Jesus and Mary Chain, Supergrass; drumming 'characterized as furious, drawing comparisons to Keith Moon'.

title: Gary Young (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: 3 May 1953 - 17 Aug 2023. Original drummer of Pavement 1989-1993; recorded Slay Tracks at his Louder Than You Think studio; No. 42 in Stylus Magazine's 50 Greatest Rock Drummers.

title: Jon Wurster - Wikipedia
notes: b. 31 Oct 1966. Superchunk (every album from No Pocky on), the Mountain Goats, Bob Mould; a 1989 session produced by Steve Jordan he calls crucial to his development.

title: Dominic Howard - Wikipedia
notes: b. 7 Dec 1977, Stockport. Co-founder and drummer of Muse; left-handed kit; Mike Portnoy cited him as an influence, likening his playing to the 'groove and power' of Dave Grohl.

title: Charly Alberti - Wikipedia
notes: Carlos Ficicchia, b. 27 March 1963, Buenos Aires; son of jazz drummer Tito Alberti. Co-founded Soda Stereo in 1982, a fan of the Police; with them until 1997.

title: Soda Stereo - Wikipedia
notes: Argentine rock band 1982-1997: Gustavo Cerati, Zeta Bosio, Charly Alberti. The best-selling Argentine band of all time; new wave and ska on the debut, post-punk on Nada personal, Signos and Doble Vida; 'De Música Ligera' (Canción Animal, 1990) their best-known song in Latin America.

title: F.M. Einheit - Wikipedia
notes: Frank-Martin Strauß, b. 18 Dec 1958, Dortmund. Percussionist of Einstürzende Neubauten on 'self-designed custom instruments', mostly metal and tools such as a hammer drill; 'instrumental to the development of the sound of the group'; Abwärts, Palais Schaumburg.

title: David Sandström - Wikipedia
notes: b. 2 Jan 1975. Drummer of Swedish hardcore band Refused; later solo and AC4.

title: The Shape of Punk to Come - Wikipedia
notes: Refused's third album (1998); moved from punk towards experimental, jazz and electronic influences; 'inspiring many later artists in a wide range of genres'; Kerrang! No. 13 of the 50 Most Influential Albums (2003).
